title: Prove sharp zero-phase witness length 2n+2 for n=2 mod 4 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof: for every n=4k+2>=2, the shortest tuple in F2^n with zero nonconstant quadratic phase and full affine span has exactly 2n+2 columns. The new unbounded domain starts at n=6, with an explicit 14-column witness. This answers the zero-character part of the other-axis-residues question in Ali Romman's #5635.

```text
n = 4k+2
f <= 2n+1: impossible by a two-coset Gaussian-integer sum
f = 2n+2: attained by k eight-column code blocks and a six-column block
```

Using the cited #5635 cuspidal cancellation lemma, its fixed zero-phase residual first becomes visible at `L_r=2n+2+((r-(2n+2)) mod 4)`. At six axes these widths are `(16,17,14,15)` in residue order `(0,1,2,3)`. These are first-visible widths of that residual, not claimed complete representation-kernel thresholds. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Ali Romman #5635/#5369/#5529/#5622, Joseph Anglada #5542, Hiroki KUMAZAKI #5522, Mihir Srivastava #5521, Jose Manuel, ywz65, Chris R and the retained native/phase lineage. Doubly-even codes, character orthogonality, Gauss sums and Green's character theorem are classical. No global literature-priority claim is made. Predecessor results are cited and built on, not audited or replayed.

## Evidence

Before: #5635 settles the n=1 mod 4 family and explicitly leaves the other axis-count residues open. After: the written proof settles the exact zero-phase length for n=2 mod 4, with a source-bound standalone verifier.

Local CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized checks pass with identical receipts. Each registered command takes about 0.17 seconds, below its 120-second limit. The finite checks enumerate 132 padded witnesses through n=130, 20 independent literal-column witnesses, 1,092 codewords, 33 exact Gaussian-integer contradictions, two other-residue controls and 18 rejection controls. The complete ordered two-axis census covers 5,461 tuples and 174,752 literal phase checks, with exactly 90 full-span zero-phase tuples at length six and none shorter. No six-axis exhaustive census is claimed.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/zero-phase-even-residue
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/zero-phase-even-residue --check-source-history --check-modes
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/zero-phase-even-residue/verify.py
```

On another machine substitute a CPython 3.12 executable. Standard library only. Expected markers are `PASS_ZERO_PHASE_EVEN_RESIDUE`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

Metadata/pins, committed bytes and modes, full source-history preflight, official export integrity with declared-input coverage, and warning-strict normal/optimized replay from a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH all pass at `dedb8bd4a53ecf7b36975941a872173ed8f2a1ba`. All nine exported files, including the export manifest, retain their bytes and modes. An actual cited-source corruption is rejected. The verifier emits hash-bound receipts and writes no files.

Base and final upstream refresh are canonical main `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19216168). Live PR/Discussion checks and separate main/merged searches found no matching published result; sparse local notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain overlap limits.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

This is a scoped written proof with finite corroboration. The residual corollary inherits #5635's cuspidal cancellation lemma and its classical character-theory input. No large affine group or complete phase-character family is enumerated. The all-character upper bound, complete native cutoff, efficient residual expansion, physical inputs/returns, paid invoice, compiler, precision, tapes and stock remain open. All five framework assumptions retain their status. No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human acceptance or formal proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Related open work

No open PR found in the refreshed published search computes this zero-phase tuple minimum or its residual's first-visible widths. Nearby work has distinct scopes:

- #5883 proves a lower Gram bound for the full Clifford tensor family; it does not compute monomial zero-phase tuple lengths.
- #5843 studies identity scratch in monomial two-FULL routing; its graded rank obstruction is a different invariant.
- #5891 permits scratch-reading FULL shears in that routing problem; it does not determine a native tensor test cutoff.
- #5837 and #5894 concern all-column lifting and existing phase-check coverage for selected P104 maps; this package is an algebraic zero-character construction, with no selected operator replay.

- #5903 computes the exact COPY approximation error for a fixed constant-weight phase-history alphabet. It shares Gaussian monomial tensor operators, but its response projection error differs from this package's zero-phase tuple length and first-visible residual width.

Completion refresh inspected this account's nine other open PRs created since the advance CLAIM: #5897, #5898, #5899, #5900, #5901, #5903, #5904, #5905 and #5906. The phase-history relationship with #5903 is recorded above. The other contributions study contiguous helper storage, clean bank exchange, tail-gate block length, Newton residual precision, invoice frontiers, dyadic observation acquisition, one-pass child buffering and a fixed two-burst query schedule. None computes this zero-phase tuple minimum or this residual's first-visible widths. No common-instance numerical disagreement was identified; no extra mathematical computations were run to validate or compare their results.

## Open next questions

- Does every phase character have a full-affine-span realization at the proposed six-axis widths? Start with affine character-orbit reduction and a checked constructive upper bound. The present result only handles the zero character.
- What are the complete native test cutoffs in the remaining higher-axis residue classes? A matching all-character upper certificate is required; an attaining zero-phase tuple alone is insufficient.

## CI notes

The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40501260249/job/122179225197) lasted 10m03s and was cancelled at its ten-minute job time limit while `actions/checkout` was still running the repository `git fetch`. Its checkout log reaches `Fetching the repository`, starts `git fetch`, and ends with `The operation was canceled.` Setup Python, onboarding tests and package selection were all skipped. No repository check or package command ran.

Separately, canonical main `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a` has the known shared onboarding-test failure reported across recent PRs. Direct inspection of [PR #5904's plan log](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40501296498/job/122179355240) confirms ten failure/error entries in unchanged `tests/test_research_current_assignment.py`, ending `FAILED (failures=8, errors=2, skipped=22)`. The two errors are `KeyError: 'follow_up_steps'` and `KeyError: 'catalog_first_step'`; the eight assertions concern frozen-card/current-route metadata, missing references and sparse path expectations. This is a separate main-base issue, not the failure reached by this PR's checkout-cancelled run. No rerun, empty commit or shared-file change was made.

The [replay job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40501260249/job/122183624560) was skipped. **Hosted replay has not certified this package; only the local scientific and publication checks listed above have run.** Local normal, optimized, registered, committed-byte/mode/source-history and read-only export checks passed. The hosted status is not scientific acceptance.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. The change is an isolated research package.

Blast radius: local. Shared code, frozen sources and selected-frontier files are unchanged.
